modules.title: 1. Account Setup & Interface Overview
modules.content:
## Getting Started – From a Blank Screen to Your First Monday.com Account  

Imagine you’ve just been handed the reins of a small marketing team that works across three time zones. Your manager wants a single place to track campaign ideas, assign tasks, and see progress at a glance—but you’ve never used Monday.com before. The first question that pops up isn’t “How do I build a board?”; it’s “How do I even get inside the platform?”  

This chapter walks you through that exact moment: creating a Monday.com account, picking a plan that matches a beginner’s needs, and learning the layout of the interface so you can feel comfortable navigating the tool from day one.

---

## 1. Creating a Monday.com Account  

### 1.1 The Sign‑Up Flow  

1. **Visit the homepage** – Go to **[monday.com](https://monday.com)**. The landing page greets you with a brief value proposition and a prominent **“Start for free”** button.  
2. **Enter your email** – Type the email address you’ll use for work (or a personal email if you’re just testing). Monday.com will automatically detect whether the domain belongs to a known company and may suggest a pre‑filled workspace name.  
3. **Choose a password** – Create a strong password (at least 8 characters, a mix of letters, numbers, and symbols). Monday.com offers a strength meter to guide you.  
4. **Confirm your email** – Check your inbox for a verification message and click the link inside. This step protects your account from unauthorized access.  
5. **Answer a quick onboarding questionnaire** – You’ll be asked about the size of your team, the type of work you do, and whether you’re looking for a personal or team solution. The answers help Monday.com suggest the most relevant features, but you can skip or edit them later.  

> **Tip:** If you already have a Google or Microsoft account, you can click the corresponding **“Sign up with Google”** or **“Sign up with Microsoft”** button. This creates a Monday.com account linked to your existing credentials, saving you a password to remember.

### 1.2 Verifying Your Identity (Optional but Recommended)  

For added security, especially if you’ll be handling sensitive data, enable **Two‑Factor Authentication (2FA)** after logging in:

- Navigate to **Profile → Settings → Security**.  
- Choose either an authentication app (e.g., Authy, Google Authenticator) or SMS codes.  
- Follow the on‑screen prompts to scan a QR code or receive a text message.  

Once 2FA is active, each login will require the second factor, dramatically reducing the risk of unauthorized entry.

---

## 2. Choosing the Right Plan for a Beginner  

Monday.com offers several subscription tiers, each unlocking a different set of features. As a beginner, you’ll likely start with the **Free** or **Basic** plan and upgrade as your needs evolve.

| Plan | Cost (per user, billed annually) | Core Features | Ideal For |
|------|----------------------------------|---------------|-----------|
| **Free** | $0 | Unlimited boards, 2 team members, limited column types, basic integrations | Solo users, hobby projects, evaluation |
| **Basic** | ≈ $8 | Unlimited boards, 5 team members, unlimited column types, simple automations, unlimited items | Small teams (2‑5 members) needing a bit more flexibility |
| **Standard** | ≈ $10 | Everything in Basic + timeline & Gantt views, calendar view, advanced automations, 250 automations per month | Growing teams that need visual planning |
| **Pro** | ≈ $16 | Everything in Standard + workload management, private boards, 25 K automation runs, advanced reporting | Larger teams with complex workflows |
| **Enterprise** | Custom pricing | All features + dedicated support, SSO, advanced security, custom contracts | Large organizations with strict compliance needs |

**Why the Free or Basic plan is usually enough for beginners**

- **No financial commitment** – The Free plan lets you explore without spending a cent.  
- **Simplicity** – Fewer column types and automations mean less to learn initially.  
- **Scalability** – Upgrading later is a single click; all your data and boards migrate automatically.  

### 2.1 Selecting a Plan During Sign‑Up  

When you finish the onboarding questionnaire, Monday.com will propose a plan based on your answers. You can:

- **Accept the recommendation** – Click **“Start with Free”** or **“Upgrade to Basic”**.  
- **Explore other options** – Click the **“Change plan”** link at the bottom of the screen to view the full pricing table.  

If you’re unsure, select **Free** and later navigate to **Admin → Billing** to switch plans. The transition is seamless; you won’t lose any boards or items.

### 2.2 Trial Periods and Money‑Back Guarantees  

Monday.com often offers a **14‑day free trial** of the paid plans. During the trial you have full access to the features of the selected tier. If you decide the plan isn’t right, you can downgrade before the trial ends without any charge.  

> **Caution:** Once the trial expires, the system automatically converts you to a paid subscription unless you manually downgrade. Set a calendar reminder a few days before the trial ends to avoid surprise charges.

---

## 3. Navigating the Main Interface  

After you log in, the screen is split into three primary zones: the **Sidebar**, the **Top Bar**, and the **Workspace Selector**. Understanding each zone will let you move around confidently.

### 3.1 The Sidebar – Your Navigation Hub  

Located on the left edge, the Sidebar contains icons and labels that serve as shortcuts to the most frequently used sections.

| Icon | Label | What It Opens |
|------|-------|---------------|
| 🏠 | **Home** | A personal dashboard that aggregates activity from all your workspaces. |
| 📂 | **Workspaces** | A list of all workspaces you belong to; clicking a workspace reveals its boards. |
| 📊 | **Dashboards** | Visual summaries (charts, graphs) that pull data from multiple boards. |
| 📥 | **Inbox** | A centralized place for notifications, mentions, and updates. |
| ⚙️ | **Admin** (visible only to admins) | Settings for billing, users, permissions, and security. |
| ❓ | **Help Center** | Access to tutorials, community forums, and live chat support. |

**Customizing the Sidebar**

- **Collapse/Expand** – Click the thin arrow at the top of the Sidebar to hide or reveal the labels, giving you more screen real estate.  
- **Reorder items** – Drag an icon up or down to prioritize the sections you use most.  
- **Pin frequently used boards** – Hover over a board name in the **Workspaces** area and click the pin icon; the board will appear at the top of the Sidebar for one‑click access.

### 3.2 The Top Bar – Search, Notifications, and Profile  

Stretching across the width of the screen, the Top Bar houses tools you’ll use almost every day.

1. **Global Search** – The magnifying glass at the far left lets you type keywords (board names, item titles, column values) and instantly jump to the matching result.  
2. **Quick Add (+)** – Next to the search field, the **“+”** button opens a menu to create a new board, item, or workspace without leaving your current view.  
3. **Notifications Bell** – Shows a red badge with the number of unread notifications. Clicking it reveals a dropdown with recent activity, mentions, and system alerts.  
4. **Help & Resources** – A question‑mark icon opens the Help Center, where you can search tutorials or start a live chat with support.  
5 **Profile Avatar** – Your photo or initials sit on the far right. Clicking opens a mini‑menu with **Profile**, **Settings**, **Logout**, and **Switch Account** options.  

### 3.3 Workspace Selector – Organizing Your Work Across Teams  

A **workspace** is a container that groups related boards, dashboards, and members. Think of it as a “project folder” that can be dedicated to a department, a client, or a specific initiative.

- **Locating the selector** – Directly under the **Home** icon in the Sidebar, you’ll see the name of the current workspace (e.g., **“Marketing Team”**) with a downward arrow.  
- **Switching workspaces** – Click the arrow to reveal a dropdown of all workspaces you belong to. Selecting another workspace instantly loads its contents.  
- **Creating a new workspace** – At the bottom of the dropdown, click **“+ New Workspace”**. You’ll be prompted to name it, choose a color, and set its privacy (public within your organization or private to invited members only).  

> **Scenario:** *You’re working on a product launch while also supporting the ongoing social media calendar. By placing the launch boards in a “Product Launch” workspace and the social media boards in a “Social Media” workspace, you can quickly toggle between the two contexts without cluttering a single view.*

---

## 4. Personalizing Your Profile  

A well‑filled profile not only makes you recognizable to teammates but also ensures that Monday.com respects your preferences for time zones, language, and accessibility.

### 4.1 Editing Core Profile Information  

1. Click your **avatar** in the Top Bar and choose **“Profile”**.  
2. On the profile page, you’ll see fields for **Full Name**, **Job Title**, **Phone Number**, and **Location**.  
3. Upload a **profile picture** by dragging an image onto the circular placeholder or clicking **“Upload photo.”**  
4. Set your **Time Zone** – Important for deadline calculations and automatic timestamp conversions.  

All changes are saved automatically; there’s no “Save” button.

### 4.2 Language and Accessibility Settings  

- **Language** – In **Profile → Settings → General**, select your preferred language from a dropdown (English, Spanish, French, etc.). Monday.com updates the interface instantly.  
- **Accessibility** – Under **Settings → Accessibility**, you can enable **High‑Contrast Mode**, increase **Font Size**, or turn on **Keyboard Navigation** shortcuts. These options help users with visual impairments or those who prefer a keyboard‑only workflow.  

---

## 5. Managing Notification Preferences  

Receiving the right amount of information is crucial. Too many alerts can drown you; too few can leave you unaware of critical updates. Monday.com offers granular control over **email**, **in‑app**, and **mobile push** notifications.

### 5.1 Types of Notifications  

| Channel | Typical Use |
|---------|-------------|
| **Email** | Summaries of daily activity, missed mentions, and system alerts (e.g., password changes). |
| **In‑App** | Real‑time pop‑ups that appear in the **Inbox** while you’re logged in. |
| **Mobile Push** | Alerts that appear on your phone’s lock screen (requires the mobile app). |

### 5.2 Configuring Global Notification Settings  

1. Click your **avatar → Settings → Notifications**.  
2. You’ll see three tabs: **Email**, **In‑App**, and **Mobile**.  
3. For each tab, toggle switches for categories such as **Mentions**, **Assignments**, **Status Changes**, and **Comment Replies**.  

**Example configuration for a beginner:**  

- **Email:** Enable **Mentions** and **Assignments** only; disable daily digests to avoid inbox overload.  
- **In‑App:** Keep **All** notifications on while you’re learning the platform, so you don’t miss anything.  
- **Mobile:** Turn on **Mentions** only if you need real‑time alerts while away from your computer.  

### 5.3 Workspace‑Specific Notification Overrides  

Sometimes a particular workspace (e.g., a fast‑moving sales pipeline) requires more frequent updates than others. To adjust settings per workspace:

1. Open the workspace from the **Sidebar**.  
2. Click the **gear icon** next to the workspace name and select **“Notification Settings.”**  
3. Choose **“Use global settings”** (default) or **“Customize for this workspace.”**  
4. If customizing, you can, for example, enable **All** in‑app notifications for the sales workspace while keeping them muted elsewhere.  

### 5.4 Do Not Disturb (DND) Mode  

When you need focused time—perhaps while drafting a project brief—you can activate **Do Not Disturb**:

- Click the **bell icon** in the Top Bar.  
- Select **“Do Not Disturb”** and choose a duration (15 minutes, 1 hour, 2 hours, or **“Until I turn it off.”**)  

During DND, all in‑app and push notifications are silenced, but email alerts continue unless you also disable them in the **Email** tab. The bell icon turns gray to indicate the mode is active.

---

## 6. Quick Tips for a Smooth Start  

- **Bookmark the Home dashboard** – It provides a quick overview of all activity across workspaces.  
- **Pin your most‑used boards** – Use the Sidebar pin feature to keep them within reach.  
- **Set a profile picture early** – It helps teammates recognize you in comments and mentions.  
- **Start with the Free plan** – You can always upgrade later; there’s no penalty for exploring.  
- **Enable 2FA** – A small step that adds a big security boost, especially for team accounts.  

---

## Key Takeaways  

- **Account creation** is a simple three‑step process: email entry, password setup, and email verification.  
- **Beginner‑friendly plans** (Free or Basic) provide enough functionality to start without a financial commitment.  
- The **Sidebar**, **Top Bar**, and **Workspace Selector** form the core navigation framework; mastering them lets you move between projects effortlessly.  
- **Personal profile settings**—photo, job title, time zone, language, and accessibility—are edited from the avatar menu and saved automatically.  
- **Notification preferences** can be tailored globally and per workspace, with separate controls for email, in‑app, and mobile alerts.  
- **Do Not Disturb** offers a quick way to silence interruptions while you focus on deep work.  

With your account set up, plan chosen, and interface familiar, you’re ready to dive into the next chapter: **Understanding Workspaces and Boards**. Happy organizing!

modules.title: 2. Understanding Workspaces and Boards
modules.content:
## The Building Blocks of Monday.com: Workspaces, Boards, and Groups  

Imagine you’ve just been hired to coordinate the launch of a new product line. Your team includes designers, engineers, marketers, and sales reps—each with their own tasks, deadlines, and files. How do you keep everyone’s work visible, separate, yet still part of the same overall project? In Monday.com, the answer lies in the three‑tier hierarchy of **Workspaces → Boards → Groups**. Think of it as a set of nested containers, each serving a distinct purpose:

| Level | What it Holds | Typical Use | Who Can See It |
|-------|---------------|-------------|----------------|
| **Workspace** | One or more Boards | A logical collection of related projects (e.g., “Product Launch 2024”) | All members you invite to the workspace |
| **Board** | Items (rows) organized into Columns | A single project, workflow, or process (e.g., “Design Sprint – Phase 1”) | Everyone in the workspace, unless the board is set to *private* |
| **Group** | A subset of items within a board | Stages, categories, or teams (e.g., “To‑Do”, “In Review”, “Completed”) | Same audience as the board itself |

Understanding how these pieces fit together is the first step toward turning Monday.com into a digital command center for your work.

---

## 1. Workspaces: Your Top‑Level Hub  

### 1.1 What Is a Workspace?  

A **workspace** is the highest‑level container in Monday.com. It groups together boards that belong to the same department, client, product line, or any other logical collection you choose. Because workspaces sit directly under your account, they inherit the same subscription plan (Free, Basic, Standard, etc.) you selected during **Account Setup & Interface Overview**.

### 1.2 Why Use Multiple Workspaces?  

- **Separation of concerns** – Keep the marketing team’s boards distinct from engineering’s, avoiding clutter.  
- **Permission control** – Invite only the relevant people to each workspace, limiting access to sensitive data.  
- **Reporting clarity** – Generate workspace‑level analytics to see how each business unit is performing.

### 1.3 Creating Your First Workspace  

1. **Navigate to the left‑hand sidebar** (the navigation panel you saw after signing in).  
2. Click **“+ New Workspace”** at the bottom of the list.  
3. **Name your workspace** – e.g., *“Product Launch 2024”*.  
4. (Optional) Add a short **description** to remind members of its purpose.  
5. Click **“Create”**.

> **Tip:** If you’re on the Free plan, you can create up to three workspaces. Upgrade to Basic or higher for unlimited workspaces.

### 1.4 Inviting Team Members to a Workspace  

1. Open the workspace you just created.  
2. Select the **“Members”** tab (usually a silhouette icon at the top of the workspace view).  
3. Click **“Invite”** and type the email addresses of teammates.  
4. Choose a **role** for each invitee:  
   - **Admin** – Full control over workspace settings and all boards.  
   - **Member** – Can view and edit boards but cannot change workspace permissions.  
5. Press **“Send Invite”**. Invited users receive an email with a link to join the workspace.

> **Scenario:** Maya, the product manager, creates a *“Product Launch 2024”* workspace and invites the design lead, the engineering lead, and the marketing coordinator. Each receives a single invitation that automatically adds them to the workspace, giving them instant visibility into all upcoming launch boards.

---

## 2. Boards: The Core Work Surface  

### 2.1 Defining a Board  

A **board** is where the actual work happens. It consists of **items** (rows) that represent tasks, projects, or any unit of work, and **columns** that capture attributes such as status, owner, due date, or files. Boards live inside a workspace and inherit its member list unless you modify the board’s privacy settings.

### 2.2 Board Types: Main, Private, and Shareable  

| Type | Visibility | Typical Use | Who Can Access |
|------|------------|-------------|----------------|
| **Main (default)** | All workspace members | General project tracking | Everyone in the workspace |
| **Private** | Only invited members (can be outside the workspace) | Confidential initiatives, HR processes | Specific users you select |
| **Shareable** | Anyone with the link (view‑only unless they have edit rights) | External stakeholders, clients | Anyone you share the link with |

- **Main boards** are the most common; they promote collaboration within the workspace.  
- **Private boards** are useful when a project involves sensitive data that only a subset of people should see.  
- **Shareable boards** let you give clients or partners a window into progress without granting them full account access.

### 2.3 Adding a New Board  

1. Inside the desired workspace, click **“+ New Board”** at the top‑right.  
2. **Enter a board name** – e.g., *“Design Sprint – Phase 1”*.  
3. Choose a **board type** (Main, Private, Shareable).  
4. (Optional) Select a **template** from the library if you want pre‑configured columns (e.g., “Project Management”).  
5. Click **“Create Board”**.

> **Quick Check:** If you later discover the board should be private, you can change its type from the board settings (gear icon) → **“Change board type.”**  

### 2.4 Board Settings You’ll Use Early On  

- **Board Description** – A short paragraph that explains the board’s purpose.  
- **Board Owner** – Usually the person who created the board; can be reassigned.  
- **Permissions** – Adjust who can edit, view, or delete items.  
- **Column Management** – Add, hide, or reorder columns to match your workflow.

---

## 3. Groups: Organizing Items Within a Board  

### 3.1 What Is a Group?  

A **group** is a visual subsection of a board that clusters related items. Think of groups as “folders” inside a board, helping you segment work by stage, team, or any logical division.

### 3.2 Common Grouping Strategies  

- **By workflow stage** – *“Backlog”, “In Progress”, “Done”* (Kanban style).  
- **By department** – *“Design Team”, “Engineering Team”, “Marketing Team”*.  
- **By sprint or timeframe** – *“Sprint 1 (Jan 1‑15)”, “Sprint 2 (Jan 16‑31)”*.  

### 3.3 Creating and Managing Groups  

1. Open a board.  
2. Click **“+ Add Group”** at the bottom of the existing groups list.  
3. **Name the group** (e.g., “To‑Do”).  
4. Drag and drop items between groups to reorganize them.  

You can also **duplicate** a group (hover over the group name, click the three‑dot menu → “Duplicate”) or **collapse** it to save screen space.

> **Example:** On the *“Design Sprint – Phase 1”* board, the product manager creates three groups: *“Ideas”, “Design Review”,* and *“Approved”.* As designers submit concepts, the PM moves items from “Ideas” to “Design Review,” and finally to “Approved” once the stakeholder signs off.

---

## 4. Putting It All Together: A Step‑by‑Step Walkthrough  

Below is a concise, end‑to‑end example that ties together workspace creation, member invitation, board setup, and group organization.

1. **Create a Workspace**  
   - Name: *“Product Launch 2024”*  
   - Description: “All boards related to the upcoming product line.”  

2. **Invite Core Team Members**  
   - Maya (Product Manager) – Admin  
   - Alex (Design Lead) – Member  
   - Priya (Engineering Lead) – Member  
   - Sam (Marketing Coordinator) – Member  

3. **Add Three Main Boards**  
   - *“Design Sprint – Phase 1”* (Main) – Template: Project Management  
   - *“Engineering Development”* (Main) – Template: Timeline  
   - *“Marketing Campaign”* (Main) – Template: Campaign Tracker  

4. **Configure the “Design Sprint – Phase 1” Board**  
   - **Groups:**  
     - *Ideas*  
     - *Design Review*  
     - *Approved*  
   - **Columns:**  
     - Status (Dropdown)  
     - Owner (People)  
     - Due Date (Date)  
     - Attachments (Files)  

5. **Set Permissions** (optional)  
   - Keep the board as a Main board so all workspace members can see it.  
   - If a confidential prototype needs a Private board, create a new Private board under the same workspace and invite only Alex and Maya.

6. **Start Adding Items**  
   - In the *Ideas* group, Alex adds “Concept A” and “Concept B” with initial sketches attached.  

7. **Move Items Through Groups**  
   - As concepts pass review, Maya drags “Concept A” to *Design Review* and later to *Approved* once signed off.

This workflow illustrates the hierarchy in action: the *workspace* houses everything, each *board* focuses on a distinct discipline, and *groups* break down the board’s items into manageable sections.

---

## 5. Best Practices for Beginners  

- **Start simple:** Create one workspace per major project or department. Add a few Main boards before experimenting with Private or Shareable boards.  
- **Name consistently:** Use a naming convention that reflects hierarchy, e.g., *Workspace – Board – Group* (e.g., “Product Launch 2024 – Design Sprint – Ideas”).  
- **Invite strategically:** Give Admin rights only to those who truly need full control. Most team members can operate as Members.  
- **Leverage templates:** The built‑in templates save time and illustrate common column setups; you can always customize them later.  
- **Use groups for visual clarity:** Even a single board can become overwhelming without groups. Break it down by stages or teams to keep the view tidy.  

---

## Key Takeaways  

- **Workspace → Board → Group** is the hierarchical structure that organizes everything in Monday.com.  
- **Workspaces** group related boards and control who can access them.  
- **Boards** are the primary work surface; they can be Main, Private, or Shareable depending on visibility needs.  
- **Groups** subdivide a board’s items, helping you track stages, teams, or time periods.  
- Creating a workspace, inviting members, adding a board, and establishing groups are the foundational actions every beginner should master before moving on to building items and columns.  

With these fundamentals in place, you’re ready to dive deeper into building your first board and customizing its columns in the next chapter.
