## Starting with a Real‑World Need  

Imagine you’ve just been tasked with launching a new product line for a small company. The marketing lead wants a single place where the team can **track ideas, assign responsibilities, set deadlines, and see the overall progress** at a glance. You’ve heard that Monday.com can serve as that hub, but you’ve never built a board before. This chapter walks you through exactly that first step: turning a blank canvas—or a ready‑made template—into a functional board that matches your project’s needs.

> **Pro tip:** If you’re still logged into the account you created in *Chapter 1 – Account Setup & Interface Overview*, you’ll see the familiar Monday.com homepage with your **Workspace** already displayed. All the actions below assume you’re starting from that view.

---

## Choosing a Starting Point: Template vs. Blank Board  

### When a Template Makes Sense  

Templates are pre‑configured boards that come with a set of columns, default views, and sample items. They save you time when the underlying structure matches a common workflow—project management, sales pipeline, event planning, etc.

**Typical scenarios for using a template**

- You need a proven structure (e.g., a Gantt‑style timeline for a construction project).  
- Your team prefers a visual that’s already familiar (e.g., Kanban board for agile teams).  
- You want to explore Monday.com’s capabilities before customizing everything yourself.

### Accessing the Template Library  

1. From the homepage, locate the **+ New** button in the upper‑right corner.  
2. Click **+ New → Board**.  
3. In the dialog that appears, choose **“Use a template”** instead of **“Start from scratch.”**  
4. Browse the categories (Project Management, CRM, Marketing, etc.) or type a keyword in the search bar.

> **Example:** For the product launch, the *“Project Management”* template provides columns like **Status**, **Timeline**, **Owner**, and **Priority**—a solid foundation for tracking tasks.

### Selecting and Instantiating a Template  

1. Click the thumbnail of the desired template.  
2. A preview screen shows the board’s layout and a short description.  
3. Hit **“Use this template.”**  
4. You’ll be prompted to **name your new board** and choose the **Workspace** where it will reside (the workspace you explored in *Chapter 2 – Understanding Workspaces and Boards*).  
5. Press **Create Board**.

Monday.com instantly generates a copy of the template, preserving the column types and any sample items the template includes. You can now start editing it to fit your specific project.

### Starting from a Blank Board  

If no template aligns with your workflow, or you prefer to build the board piece‑by‑piece, a blank board gives you full control.

1. Click **+ New → Board** again.  
2. This time select **“Start from scratch.”**  
3. Give the board a clear, descriptive name (e.g., **“Q4 Product Launch – Marketing”**) and confirm the workspace.  
4. Click **Create Board**.

You’ll see an empty grid with a single default column (usually **Name**). All further structure will be added by you.

---

## Adding and Renaming Columns  

Columns are the building blocks that define the data you capture for each item (task, idea, contact, etc.). Monday.com offers a variety of column types, each designed for a specific kind of information.

### The Most Common Column Types  

| Column Type | Typical Use | Quick Add Shortcut |
|-------------|------------|--------------------|
| **Status** | Visual progress indicator (e.g., *To Do*, *In Progress*, *Done*) | `+` → **Status** |
| **Text** | Free‑form notes, descriptions, URLs | `+` → **Text** |
| **Date** | Due dates, start dates, milestones | `+` → **Date** |
| **Person** | Assign a team member to an item | `+` → **Person** |
| **Numbers** | Budget, quantity, score | `+` → **Numbers** |
| **Dropdown** | Pre‑defined list of options (e.g., *High/Medium/Low*) | `+` → **Dropdown** |

### Step‑by‑Step: Adding Columns  

1. Hover over the far‑right edge of the board header until the **+ Add column** button appears.  
2. Click **+ Add column**.  
3. From the pop‑up menu, select the column type you need.  
4. After selection, a new column appears at the far right of the board.

**Tip:** You can drag a column header left or right to reorder it, ensuring the most important information sits at the front of the view.

### Renaming Columns  

1. Double‑click the column header text (e.g., “Status”).  
2. Type the new name (e.g., **“Launch Phase”**).  
3. Press **Enter** or click outside the header to commit the change.

Alternatively, click the three‑dot menu on the column header → **Rename column** for a more guided experience.

### Customizing Columns for the Product Launch Board  

Below is a practical column set you might assemble for the scenario introduced at the start of this chapter:

| Column | Suggested Type | Example Values |
|--------|----------------|----------------|
| **Task** | Text (default “Name” column) | “Create press release” |
| **Owner** | Person | Jane Doe |
| **Launch Phase** | Status | *Planning → Design → Review → Completed* |
| **Due Date** | Date | 2024‑09‑15 |
| **Priority** | Dropdown (High / Medium / Low) | High |
| **Budget ($)** | Numbers | 2,500 |
| **Notes** | Text (long‑form) | “Include new product tagline” |

To add each column, follow the **Adding Columns** steps above, then rename them to match the titles in the table. Populate a few sample items to see how the board feels in practice.

### Advanced Column Tweaks (Optional for Beginners)  

- **Duplicate a column:** Click the three‑dot menu on the column header → **Duplicate column**. Useful when you need a similar column with a different name (e.g., two separate date columns).  
- **Hide a column:** Same menu → **Hide column**. Hidden columns stay in the board but are not visible in the current view; you can unhide them later.  
- **Column settings:** Some column types have extra options (e.g., setting a default status label or date format). Click the three‑dot menu → **Column settings** to explore these.

---

## Configuring Basic Board Settings  

Beyond the grid itself, Monday.com lets you tailor the board’s **privacy**, **visual identity**, and **description**—all of which help teammates understand purpose and control access.

### Accessing Board Settings  

1. In the upper‑right corner of the board, click the **three‑dot (More actions) icon**.  
2. Choose **Board settings** from the dropdown.  
3. A side panel opens with several tabs: **General**, **Permissions**, **Appearance**, etc.

### Setting Board Privacy  

- **Private board:** Only invited members can view or edit. Ideal for confidential projects.  
- **Shareable board:** Anyone with the link can access (read‑only or edit depending on permission).  
- **Workspace‑wide board:** Visible to everyone in the selected workspace (default for most internal projects).

**How to change privacy**

1. In the **Permissions** tab, locate **Board visibility**.  
2. Select the desired level (e.g., **Private**).  
3. Click **Save**.  

> **Security note:** If you enabled **Two‑Factor Authentication (2FA)** in *Chapter 1*, private boards gain an extra layer of protection because only authenticated users can be invited.

### Choosing a Board Color and Icon  

A splash of color makes it easier to locate the board among many others.

1. In the **Appearance** tab, click the **Color palette** and pick a hue that matches your project theme (e.g., orange for a marketing launch).  
2. Click the **Icon selector** (a small square) to choose an emoji or icon that represents the board (e.g., 📦 for product launch).  
3. Press **Apply**.

The selected color and icon appear next to the board name on the homepage and in the workspace sidebar.

### Adding a Board Description  

A concise description tells newcomers what the board is for and how to use it.

1. Still within the **General** tab, locate the **Description** field.  
2. Type a brief overview, such as:  

   > *“This board tracks all tasks, owners, and deadlines for the Q4 product launch. Use the Status column to see which phase each task is in.”*  

3. Click **Save**.

The description is visible when teammates hover over the board name or click the **i** (information) icon on the board header.

### Inviting Team Members  

Even though inviting collaborators belongs to the next chapter on *Managing Items and Columns*, it’s useful to know the basics now.

1. Click the **Invite** button (usually at the top‑right of the board).  
2. Enter email addresses or select existing workspace members.  
3. Choose a role (Member, Viewer, etc.) and hit **Send Invite**.

Your board is now ready for collaboration.

---

## Quick Review: From Empty Canvas to Live Board  

1. **Decide** whether a template fits your workflow. If not, start with a blank board.  
2. **Add columns** that capture the data you need—Status, Date, Person, etc.  
3. **Rename columns** to reflect the language of your project.  
4. **Configure settings**: set privacy to Private, pick a color/icon, and write a helpful description.  
5. **Save** and **invite** the right people.

You’ve now created a functional Monday.com board that reflects the real‑world demands of a product launch. The next steps—adding items, customizing views, and automating processes—will build on this solid foundation.

---

## Key Takeaways  

- **Templates accelerate setup** when they align with your workflow; otherwise, a blank board gives full flexibility.  
- **Columns define the data** you’ll track; common types include Status, Date, Person, and Numbers. Add and rename them to match your project terminology.  
- **Board settings** (privacy, color, description) control who sees the board and how it’s identified within your workspace.  
- **A clear naming convention** for the board and its columns makes onboarding new teammates effortless.  
- **One board, many uses:** The same steps apply whether you’re managing a marketing campaign, a sales pipeline, or a personal to‑do list.  

Now that your first board is live, you’re ready to populate it with items and start turning ideas into actionable work.

modules.title: 4. Managing Items and Columns
modules.content:
## Adding Your First Items – The Building Blocks of a Board  

Imagine you’ve just built a new board in the “Launch Campaign” workspace (see *Building Your First Board*). The board is empty, but you already know the big picture: you need to plan the product launch, coordinate marketing, and track deliverables. The next step is to start **adding items** – the individual tasks, ideas, or pieces of work that will fill the board.

### 1. The Quick‑Add Toolbar  

At the top of every board sits the **Quick‑Add toolbar** (the plus ✚ icon next to the board name). Clicking it opens a tiny form:

1. **Enter a name** – This becomes the item’s title (e.g., “Write press release”).  
2. **Choose a group** – By default the item lands in the first group (often “Group 1”). You can switch groups later.  
3. **Press Enter** – The item appears as a new row on the board.

> **Tip:** Hover over the plus ✚ icon; a tooltip reminds you that you can also press **Enter** while a column is selected to add an item instantly.

### 2. Adding Multiple Items at Once  

If you have a list of tasks prepared in a spreadsheet, you can paste them directly:

* Copy the column of task names.  
* Click the **+ Add item** button at the bottom of the board.  
* Paste – Monday.com will create a separate item for each line.

This “bulk‑add” method is a lifesaver when you’re migrating from an old to‑do list.

### 3. Editing Item Details  

Once an item exists, click its name to open the **Item Details pane** on the right. Here you can:

* **Rename** the item.  
* **Add a description** – useful for context, links, or notes.  
* **Attach files** – drag‑and‑drop or click the paper‑clip icon.  
* **Add comments** – a lightweight way to start a conversation (covered later in the Collaboration chapter).

All changes are saved automatically; there’s no “Save” button to hunt for.

## Assigning Owners and Setting Due Dates  

Every task on a launch board needs a person responsible and a deadline. Monday.com makes both actions a single click away.

### 1. The People Column  

When you created the board, you likely added a **People** column (or you can add one now by clicking **+ Add Column → People**).  

* **Assigning an owner** – Click the empty cell in the People column for the item, then type the teammate’s name. Monday.com suggests matches from your workspace.  
* **Multiple owners** – Click again to add another name. This is handy for collaborative tasks like “Design landing page”.

### 2. The Date Column  

A **Date** column stores due dates, start dates, or any calendar‑related information.

* **Setting a due date** – Click the cell, pick a date from the calendar pop‑up, and press **Enter**.  
* **Adding a time** – Click the clock icon that appears after selecting a date to specify a time of day.  
* **Recurring dates** – While still a beginner feature, you can type “every Monday” and Monday.com will auto‑populate the next occurrences (useful for weekly check‑ins).

> **Pro tip:** Enable the **Timeline** view later (chapter 5) to see dates visualised as bars.

## Working with Column Types  

Columns are the “attributes” you attach to each item. Beyond People and Date, Monday.com offers a palette of column types that let you capture status, choices, numbers, and even calculations. Below we walk through the most common ones for beginners.

### 1. Status Column – Visual Progress Tracking  

A **Status** column displays colored labels (e.g., “To Do”, “In Progress”, “Done”).  

* **Adding a Status column** – Click **+ Add Column → Status**.  
* **Customising labels** – Click the column header, choose **Edit Labels**, then add, rename, or recolour tags.  
* **Changing an item’s status** – Click the cell and select the appropriate label. The color instantly signals progress at a glance.

**Scenario:** Your launch board includes a “Creative Assets” group. Each asset (logo, banner, video) gets a Status column with labels “Not Started”, “Designing”, “Approved”. The team can see at a glance which assets still need work.

### 2. Dropdown Column – Controlled Choice Lists  

When you need a predefined set of options (e.g., “Channel” with values “Email”, “Social”, “Paid Ads”), a **Dropdown** column is perfect.

* **Create a Dropdown column** – **+ Add Column → Dropdown**.  
* **Define options** – Click the header → **Edit Options**, then type each choice on a new line.  
* **Select an option** – Click the cell and choose from the list.

Dropdowns keep data consistent, which is crucial when you later filter or sort (chapter 5).

### 3. Numbers Column – Tracking Quantities  

A **Numbers** column records any numeric value: budgets, hours, scores, etc.

* **Add a Numbers column** – **+ Add Column → Numbers**.  
* **Set a format** – Click the header → **Column Settings** → choose currency, decimal places, or plain number.  
* **Enter a value** – Click the cell and type the number.

**Example:** In a “Budget” group, each line item (e.g., “Paid Social”) gets a Numbers column for the cost estimate.

### 4. Formula Column – Simple Calculations on the Fly  

A **Formula** column lets you compute values based on other columns. No coding required – just a few basic operators.

* **Create a Formula column** – **+ Add Column → Formula**.  
* **Write the expression** – Click the header → **Edit Formula**. Use the syntax `COLUMN_NAME` (in uppercase) to reference other columns.  

**Common formulas**  

| Goal | Formula Example |
|------|-----------------|
| Add two numbers | `{COST} + {QUANTITY}` |
| Calculate days left | `DAYS({DUE DATE}, TODAY())` |
| Show “Overdue” flag | `IF({DUE DATE} < TODAY(), "⚠️ Overdue", "On Track")` |

> **Note:** Column names that contain spaces must be wrapped in curly braces (`{Due Date}`).

Formula columns are read‑only; they update automatically whenever the referenced columns change.

## Moving Items Between Groups  

Groups are the horizontal sections that help you organise items (e.g., “To Do”, “In Progress”, “Done”). As work advances, you’ll need to shift items from one group to another.

### 1. Drag‑and‑Drop  

* Click and hold the **item’s handle** (the six‑dot icon at the far left of the row).  
* Drag the item to the target group’s header and release.  

The item instantly appears in the new group, preserving all column data.

### 2. Bulk Move  

When many items need moving:

1. **Select multiple items** – Click the checkbox next to each row, or press **Shift** and click the first and last rows to select a range.  
2. Click the **Move to group** button that appears above the board.  
3. Choose the destination group from the dropdown.

### 3. Using the “Move to” Action in the Item Details Pane  

Open an item’s details pane, click the three‑dot menu (⋮) and choose **Move to group**. This method is handy if you’re already editing the item’s description and want to relocate it without leaving the pane.

## Duplicating Items – When Templates Save Time  

Often you’ll find yourself creating very similar tasks – for instance, “Draft blog post #1”, “Draft blog post #2”, etc. Rather than typing each one from scratch, duplicate an existing item.

### 1. Single‑Item Duplicate  

1. Hover over the item’s row, click the three‑dot menu (⋮).  
2. Select **Duplicate**.  
3. Choose whether to copy **sub‑items**, **updates**, and **files** (keep them off for a clean template).  
4. Click **Duplicate** – a copy appears directly below the original with “Copy of” prefixed to the title. Rename it as needed.

### 2. Bulk Duplicate  

Select several items (checkboxes) and click the **Duplicate** button that appears in the bulk‑action bar. This creates a copy of each selected row, preserving their column values.

### 3. Using a “Template” Item  

Create a dedicated **template item** in a “Templates” group. Fill in all the columns you usually need (status set to “Not Started”, due date left blank, etc.). When a new task is required, duplicate the template and move the copy to the appropriate working group.

## Best‑Practice Tips for Beginners  

* **Name items clearly** – The title is the primary identifier; include verbs (“Create”, “Review”) and a concise object (“Landing Page”).  
* **Keep column usage consistent** – If you use a Dropdown for “Channel” in one board, reuse the same column type and options across other boards to avoid confusion.  
* **Leverage colour** – Status labels and column colours provide instant visual cues. Use them sparingly (no more than 4‑5 colours per board) to maintain clarity.  
* **Avoid over‑columning** – Start with the essential columns (People, Date, Status). Add extra columns only when you notice a recurring data need.  
* **Use bulk actions early** – Selecting multiple items and applying an edit (e.g., assign the same owner) reduces repetitive clicks.  
* **Regularly review group structure** – If a group becomes a catch‑all (“Misc”), consider splitting it into more meaningful categories.

## Putting It All Together – A Mini‑Walkthrough  

Let’s walk through a realistic scenario from start to finish, applying everything covered so far.

### Scenario: Planning a Product Launch  

1. **Create groups** – In the “Launch Campaign” board, add three groups:  
   * **Pre‑Launch**  
   * **Launch Day**  
   * **Post‑Launch**  

2. **Add items** – Use Quick‑Add to create the following tasks in **Pre‑Launch**:  
   * “Write press release”  
   * “Design hero banner”  
   * “Set up email campaign”  

3. **Assign owners** – Click the People column for each task and assign:  
   * Sarah (Marketing) → Press release  
   * Alex (Design) → Hero banner  
   * Maya (Growth) → Email campaign  

4. **Set due dates** – In the Date column, choose:  
   * Press release – May 10  
   * Hero banner – May 12  
   * Email campaign – May 15  

5. **Add a Status column** – Labels: “Not Started”, “In Progress”, “Done”. Set each task to “Not Started”.

6. **Add a Dropdown column called “Channel”** – Options: “Press”, “Social”, “Email”. Assign:  
   * Press release → Press  
   * Hero banner → Social  
   * Email campaign → Email  

7. **Add a Numbers column “Estimated Hours”** – Enter:  
   * Press release – 4  
   * Hero banner – 6  
   * Email campaign – 3  

8. **Create a Formula column “Total Effort”** – Formula: `{ESTIMATED HOURS} * 1` (simple placeholder). This shows the same number but demonstrates how formulas work.

9. **Move the completed items** – As Sarah finishes the press release, drag the row to the **Launch Day** group and change its Status to “Done”.

10. **Duplicate a template** – Create a “Template – Social Post” item in a “Templates” group with generic fields (Status = “Not Started”, Channel = “Social”). When a new social post is needed, duplicate the template, rename it (“Instagram teaser”), assign the owner, and set the due date.

Through these steps the board now holds a clear, colour‑coded roadmap, each task linked to a person, date, and effort estimate—all visible at a glance.

## Common Beginner Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them  

| Pitfall | Why It Happens | Fix |
|---------|----------------|-----|
| **Over‑loading a single item with too many columns** | Trying to capture every piece of data in one row. | Split complex data into **sub‑items** (covered later) or create a separate “Details” group. |
| **Leaving the People column empty** | Assuming “unassigned” is acceptable. | Set a default owner for each group (e.g., a project manager) to ensure accountability. |
| **Using too many Status labels** | Adding a new colour for each nuance. | Stick to 3‑5 core statuses; use comments or a custom text column for finer detail. |
| **Copy‑pasting dates without format** | Pasting “05/10/2024” from a spreadsheet that Monday.com interprets as text. | Use the **Date picker** or paste in ISO format (YYYY‑MM‑DD). |
| **Forgetting to move items after completion** | Items stay in “To Do” and clutter the board. | Make moving items a habit; consider a simple automation later (chapter 6). |

## Quick Reference Cheat Sheet  

| Action | Where to Find It | Keyboard Shortcut (if any) |
|--------|------------------|----------------------------|
| Add a new item | + Add item button or Quick‑Add toolbar | **Enter** while a column is selected |
| Edit item name/description | Click the item → right‑hand pane | — |
| Assign owner | People column cell | — |
| Set due date | Date column cell | — |
| Change status | Status column cell | — |
| Move item to another group | Drag the row’s handle or bulk‑move button | — |
| Duplicate an item | Row menu (⋮) → Duplicate | — |
| Add a new column | + Add Column at far right of header row | — |
| Select multiple rows | Checkboxes or **Shift + Click** | — |

---

## Key Takeaways  

* **Items are the fundamental units** of work on a board; add them via the Quick‑Add toolbar or bulk‑paste from a spreadsheet.  
* **People and Date columns** give each task an owner and a deadline—essential for accountability and scheduling.  
* **Status, Dropdown, Numbers, and Formula columns** let you visualise progress, enforce consistent choices, track quantitative data, and perform simple calculations.  
* **Moving items between groups** (drag‑and‑drop or bulk actions) reflects workflow changes; keep groups purposeful and limited.  
* **Duplicating items** saves time when you need repeatable task structures; maintain a “Template” item for quick reuse.  
* **Best practices** include clear naming, consistent column use, judicious colour coding, and regular housekeeping of groups and items.  

With these tools in hand, you can transform a blank board into a living, organized hub that drives your projects forward—one item at a time.

modules.title: 5. Views, Filters, and Sorting
modules.content:
## Seeing Your Work From Every Angle  

Imagine you’re managing a product launch timeline. In the **Table** view you see every task, its owner, due date, and status. When you switch to **Kanban**, the same tasks line up in columns labeled “Ideas,” “In Progress,” and “Done,” giving you a quick visual of work‑in‑progress. Flip to **Timeline** and the dates stretch across a Gantt‑style bar, revealing overlaps and bottlenecks. Finally, the **Calendar** view drops each task onto its actual due date, letting you spot busy weeks at a glance.  

All of these perspectives live on the same board—you don’t need to recreate anything. The power of Monday.com comes from being able to **toggle between views**, **filter** for exactly what you need, and **sort** items so the most relevant information bubbles to the top. Let’s walk through each step, using the product‑launch board as our running example.

---

## Switching Between Views  

Monday.com ships with several default views, each designed to answer a different question:

| View | When to Use It | What You See |
|------|----------------|--------------|
| **Table** | Detailed data entry, bulk edits | Rows (items) and columns (attributes) |
| **Kanban** | Workflow stages, visual progress | Cards stacked in columns representing statuses |
| **Timeline** | Project planning, dependencies | Bars spanning dates, optional dependencies |
| **Calendar** | Scheduling, deadline awareness | Items plotted on a monthly/weekly calendar |

### Adding a New View  

1. **Locate the View Bar** – It sits just above the board’s columns, right of the board name.  
2. Click the **“+ Add view”** button (a plus sign).  
3. Choose the view type you want (Table, Kanban, Timeline, Calendar, or any of the premium views you may have later).  
4. Give the view a descriptive name (e.g., “Launch Kanban”) and hit **Create**.  

Your new view appears as a tab next to the existing ones. Click any tab to switch instantly—no page reload required.

### Quick‑Switch Tips  

* **Keyboard shortcut:** Press **V** to open the view selector, then arrow keys to pick a view.  
* **Default view:** The first view you create becomes the board’s default when teammates open the board. You can change the default later by clicking the three‑dot menu on the view tab and selecting **Set as default**.  
* **Mobile app:** Swipe left/right on the view bar to cycle through views on a phone or tablet.

### Customizing a View  

Each view has its own settings panel (gear icon). For example, in **Timeline** you can:

* Toggle **Show weekends** on/off.  
* Enable **Dependencies** to draw arrows between tasks.  
* Adjust **Zoom level** (days, weeks, months).  

In **Kanban**, you can:

* Choose which **status column** drives the columns.  
* Enable **Group by** to stack cards by another column (e.g., “Team”).  

These customizations are saved **per view**, so your Table can stay dense while your Calendar stays clean.

---

## Applying Filters to Show Only What Matters  

Filters let you hide the noise and surface the items that matter for the moment. They work the same way across all view types, but the visual result adapts to the view you’re in.

### The Filter Bar  

1. Click the **Filter** funnel icon on the view bar.  
2. A sidebar opens with a list of all columns on your board.  
3. Choose a column, then pick an operator (e.g., **is**, **contains**, **greater than**) and enter a value.  

You can add multiple conditions; they combine with **AND** logic by default (all conditions must be true). To switch to **OR** logic, click the small **+** next to the condition list and select **Add OR condition**.

### Common Filtering Scenarios  

| Scenario | Filter Setup |
|----------|--------------|
| **Show only tasks due this week** | Column: *Due Date* → *is within* → *Next 7 days* |
| **Display items assigned to Alex** | Column: *People* → *contains* → *Alex* |
| **Hide completed items** | Column: *Status* → *is not* → *Done* |
| **Focus on high‑priority bugs** | Column: *Priority* → *is* → *High* **AND** Column: *Type* → *is* → *Bug* |

### Saving a Filtered View  

If you find yourself using the same filter repeatedly, you can **save it as a custom view** (see next section). The filter itself is also saved automatically when you create a new view, so you can have a “My Week” view that always shows only your tasks for the upcoming seven days.

### Quick‑Filter Tips  

* **Search bar:** Type a keyword into the board’s top‑right search field; Monday.com will instantly filter items across all columns that contain that text.  
* **Clear filters:** Click the **X** next to each condition or hit **Clear all** at the bottom of the filter sidebar.  
* **Pinning filters:** In a shared board, you can **pin** a filter so every teammate sees the same filtered result when they open that view. Use the three‑dot menu on the view tab → **Pin filter**.

---

## Sorting Items and Creating Custom Views  

Sorting determines the order in which items appear. While filters hide rows, sorting rearranges them. Together they make it easy to find the highest‑priority items, the nearest deadlines, or the most recent updates.

### Sorting Basics  

1. Click the **Sort** icon (looks like an A⇅Z) on the view bar.  
2. Choose a column to sort by.  
3. Select **Ascending** (A → Z, earliest → latest) or **Descending** (Z → A, latest → earliest).  

You can add a **secondary sort**—for example, first sort by *Due Date* (ascending) and then by *Priority* (descending) so that tasks due today appear at the top, with high‑priority items listed first.

### Sorting in Different Views  

* **Table view:** Items reorder in the rows directly.  
* **Kanban view:** Cards reorder within each column based on the chosen sort.  
* **Timeline view:** Sorting changes the vertical placement of bars (useful when many items share the same dates).  
* **Calendar view:** Sorting affects the order of items that fall on the same day (the most urgent appears first).

### Creating a Custom View with Filters & Sorting  

A **custom view** is a saved snapshot of a board that includes:

* The chosen view type (Table, Kanban, etc.)  
* Any active filters  
* The sorting order you defined  
* Any view‑specific settings (e.g., Kanban column grouping)

**Step‑by‑step example: “My Upcoming Tasks”**

1. Switch to **Table** view.  
2. Open the **Filter** sidebar and set:  
   * *People* **contains** *Your Name*  
   * *Status* **is not** *Done*  
   * *Due Date* **is within** *Next 14 days*  
3. Open the **Sort** panel and choose:  
   * Primary: *Due Date* → **Ascending**  
   * Secondary: *Priority* → **Descending**  
4. Click the **+ Add view** button, name the view **My Upcoming Tasks**, and hit **Create**.  

Now you have a personal dashboard that always shows the tasks you own, due soon, sorted so the most urgent appear first. Because the view is saved, you (and anyone you share it with) can return to it with a single click.

### Sharing & Managing Custom Views  

* **Sharing:** In the view tab’s three‑dot menu, select **Share view**. You can copy a link or invite teammates to view it.  
* **Permissions:** If you’re on a **Basic** or higher plan, you can set the view to **Read‑only** so others can see the filtered data but cannot modify the underlying items.  
* **Organizing:** Drag view tabs left or right to reorder them. Group related views (e.g., all Kanban‑style boards) together for quick navigation.  

### Best‑Practice Tips for Sorting & Views  

* **Limit columns** in a view to only those you need. Fewer columns mean faster loading and less visual clutter.  
* **Use colors**: Apply a **color column** (e.g., “Status”) and enable **color‑coded cards** in Kanban or Timeline; this visual cue works alongside sorting for quick scanning.  
* **Refresh wisely**: After bulk editing many items, give Monday.com a moment to re‑apply sorts—especially in large boards (hundreds of items).  

---

## Putting It All Together: A Mini‑Project  

Let’s walk through a complete workflow on a fictional “Website Redesign” board.

1. **Create the board** (covered in Chapter 3). Add columns: *Task Name*, *Owner*, *Status*, *Priority*, *Due Date*, *Tags*.  
2. **Add a Kanban view** named **Redesign Kanban**. Set the *Status* column as the board’s workflow driver.  
3. **Apply a filter** in the Kanban view: show only items where *Priority* **is** *High*. Now the team instantly sees the most critical cards.  
4. **Sort** the Kanban column by *Due Date* (ascending). The high‑priority cards are now arranged from soonest to latest.  
5. **Save this as a custom view** called **High‑Priority Sprint**. Share the link with the design lead, who can monitor the sprint without seeing low‑priority tasks.  
6. Switch to **Timeline view**, enable **Dependencies**, and **add a filter**: *Owner* **contains** *You*. Now you see only the tasks you own, plotted over the project schedule, with arrows showing which tasks depend on each other.  
7. **Create a Calendar view** called **Team Calendar** that filters on *Status* **is not** *Done*. This gives the whole team a quick glance at upcoming deadlines.  

By the end of this mini‑project, you’ve used **four different views**, **three filters**, and **two sorting orders**, each saved as a reusable view. The board now serves multiple purposes—personal task tracking, team sprint monitoring, and overall project planning—without duplicating any data.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions  

| Question | Answer |
|----------|--------|
| **Can I have more than one filter active at once?** | Yes. Add as many conditions as you need. They default to **AND** logic; you can insert **OR** blocks for more complex queries. |
| **Do filters affect other teammates?** | Filters are **view‑specific**. If you apply a filter in a personal view, only you see the filtered result. If you pin a filter to a shared view, everyone who opens that view sees the same filtered data. |
| **Will sorting change the order of items permanently?** | Sorting is **temporary** to the active view. The underlying order of items in the Table view remains unchanged unless you manually drag rows. |
| **Can I export a filtered & sorted view?** | Yes. Click the **three‑dot menu** on the view tab → **Export > Excel** (or CSV). The export respects the active filter and sort. |
| **What if I need a view that isn’t listed (e.g., a Gantt chart)?** | Monday.com offers premium view types such as **Gantt**, **Workload**, and **Chart**. You can add them the same way you add Table/Kanban, provided your subscription includes them. |

---

## Troubleshooting Tips  

* **Filter not working as expected** – Double‑check column data types. For example, a *Text* column won’t respond to “greater than” numeric operators.  
* **Sorting seems ignored** – In Kanban view, sorting only works if the board’s **Group by** setting is set to “None.” If you’ve grouped cards by another column, the group order overrides sorting.  
* **View takes too long to load** – Reduce the number of visible columns, or limit the date range in Timeline/Calendar views. Large boards (>1,000 items) may benefit from dividing work into multiple boards and linking them with **Mirror** columns.  

---

## Key Takeaways  

* **Views are lenses** – Table, Kanban, Timeline, and Calendar each reveal a different aspect of the same data. Add, name, and switch between them without duplicating items.  
* **Filters hide the noise** – Use the filter sidebar to display only the rows that meet your criteria. Combine multiple conditions with AND/OR logic and pin filters for shared visibility.  
* **Sorting orders the information** – Choose primary and secondary columns to arrange items logically; sorting works across all view types.  
* **Custom views bundle it all** – A saved view remembers the view type, active filters, sorting, and any view‑specific settings. Create personal dashboards or shared snapshots for focused work.  
* **Share, protect, and iterate** – Custom views can be shared via links, set to read‑only, and reordered for quick access.  

Mastering views, filters, and sorting turns a static board into a dynamic, personalized command center—empowering you and your team to see exactly what matters, when it matters.

modules.title: 6. Introduction to Automations
modules.content:
## Why Automate? A Real‑World Snapshot  

Imagine you’re managing a product‑launch board in Monday.com. Every time a task moves from **“In Progress”** to **“Completed,”** you need to email the project lead, update a status column, and add the item to a “Finished Tasks” view. Doing this manually for dozens of items each day wastes time and invites errors.  

**Automation** solves this problem by letting Monday.com perform those repetitive actions for you—instantly and consistently. Think of it as a “if‑this‑then‑that” engine built into every board, turning simple triggers (like a status change) into automatic outcomes (like sending a notification). With the right automation, you free up mental bandwidth to focus on strategic work instead of ticking off check‑list items.

---

## What Is an Automation?  

In Monday.com, an **automation** is a rule that connects a **trigger** (the “if” part) to an **action** (the “then” part). When the trigger condition occurs on a board, Monday.com automatically executes the defined action.  

- **Trigger** – The event that starts the automation. Common triggers include:
  - A column value changes (e.g., status, date, text)
  - An item is created or moved
  - A deadline approaches or passes
- **Action** – What Monday.com does once the trigger fires. Typical actions include:
  - Sending a notification or email
  - Updating a column value
  - Creating a new item or duplicate
  - Assigning a user or moving an item to another board

Because automations live **inside the board** you’re already working with, they respect the same permissions, views, and filters you set up in earlier chapters (see Chapters 2‑5). No separate tool or coding language is required.

---

## When to Use Automations  

| Situation | Benefit of an Automation |
|-----------|--------------------------|
| **Status changes** (e.g., “Ready for Review”) | Instantly alert the right person, avoid missed hand‑offs |
| **Upcoming deadlines** | Proactively remind owners, reduce overdue tasks |
| **Recurring tasks** (e.g., weekly reports) | Auto‑create new items, keep the rhythm without manual entry |
| **Data consistency** (e.g., keep a “Total Hours” column synced) | Reduce human error, maintain up‑to‑date numbers |
| **Cross‑board updates** (e.g., moving a lead from “Prospects” to “Clients”) | Keep multiple boards aligned without duplicate work |

If you find yourself performing the same manual steps repeatedly, an automation is likely the answer.

---

## Setting Up Your First Automation: Status‑Change Notification  

Let’s walk through a concrete example that builds on the board you created in **Chapter 3** (“Building Your First Board”). We’ll add an automation that **sends a notification to a teammate when a task’s status changes to “Done.”**  

### Step‑by‑Step Guide  

1. **Open the board** where you want the automation.  
2. In the top‑right corner, click the **Automation** button (the lightning‑bolt icon).  
3. A sidebar titled **Automation Center** appears.  
4. Click **“Create Custom Automation”** at the bottom of the list.  
5. You’ll see a simple rule builder with two placeholders:  
   - **When** … **then** …  
6. Click the **“When”** placeholder and choose **“Status changes to something.”**  
   - In the dropdown, select the **Status** column you added earlier (e.g., “Task Status”).  
   - Choose the specific status value **“Done.”**  
7. Click the **“then”** placeholder and select **“Notify someone.”**  
   - In the next field, type the name of the teammate who should receive the alert (you can also select **“Assignee”** to notify the person assigned to the item).  
   - Optionally, add a custom message, such as:  
     ```
     🎉 Task {{pulse.name}} is now Done! Please review.
     ```  
     (The double curly braces insert the item’s name automatically.)  
8. Review the rule:  

   **When** *Task Status changes to Done* **then** *Notify* *[Teammate]* *with message …*  

9. Click **“Add to Board.”** The automation now appears in the Automation Center list, marked **Active**.  

> **Tip:** If you ever need to edit the wording or the recipient, hover over the automation in the list and click the **pencil** icon.

### Testing the Automation  

1. Locate any item on your board and change its **Task Status** to **Done**.  
2. Observe the notification pop‑up in the top‑right corner (or the email, if you chose that option).  
3. Verify that the message contains the correct item name and that the intended teammate receives it.

If the notification appears as expected, the automation is working!  

---

## Managing Automation Settings  

Automations are powerful, but they can also generate noise if not tuned correctly. Monday.com gives you full control over each automation’s lifecycle.

### Viewing All Automations on a Board  

1. Click the **Automation** (lightning‑bolt) icon again.  
2. The **Automation Center** now lists every rule attached to the current board.  
3. Each automation shows a toggle switch (**On/Off**) and three icons: **Edit (pencil), Duplicate (two squares), Delete (trash can).**

### Enabling or Disabling an Automation  

- **Disable** – Flip the toggle to **Off**. The rule remains on the board but will not fire. Use this when you want a temporary pause (e.g., during a sprint retrospective).  
- **Enable** – Flip the toggle back to **On**. The rule resumes immediately.

### Editing an Automation  

1. Click the **pencil** icon next to the automation you wish to modify.  
2. The rule builder re‑opens, letting you change the trigger, action, or message.  
3. After making changes, click **“Save.”** The updated automation replaces the previous version without needing to delete and recreate it.

### Duplicating an Automation  

If you need a similar rule with a slight variation (e.g., notify a different team for a different status), click the **duplicate** icon. The copy appears in the list; edit it as needed.

### Deleting an Unwanted Automation  

1. Click the **trash can** icon.  
2. A confirmation dialog asks, “Are you sure you want to delete this automation?”  
3. Confirm to permanently remove it. Deleted automations cannot be recovered, so be sure you no longer need it.

> **Best‑practice reminder:** Keep the number of active automations low on any single board. Too many rules can make troubleshooting difficult and may affect performance on very large boards.

---

## Common Pitfalls & How to Avoid Them  

| Pitfall | Why It Happens | Fix / Prevention |
|---------|----------------|------------------|
| **Too many notifications** | Multiple automations fire for the same trigger, sending duplicate alerts. | Consolidate actions into a single automation where possible; use the **“Only once per item”** option available in some triggers. |
| **Automation not firing** | Trigger condition is too specific (e.g., wrong status value) or the column type doesn’t support the chosen trigger. | Double‑check column names and values; ensure you selected the correct column type in the trigger. |
| **Unexpected recipients** | Using “Assignee” when items have no assignee or an outdated assignee. | Add a fallback user in the action or verify that every item has a proper assignee before the automation runs. |
| **Performance lag on large boards** | Hundreds of active automations on a board with thousands of items. | Prioritize the most critical automations; move less‑used rules to a separate “Automation Hub” board and reference them via cross‑board actions (covered later in Integrations). |
| **Forgotten automations** | Over time, old automations remain active, causing confusion. | Conduct a quarterly audit: open the Automation Center, review each rule, and disable or delete those no longer needed. |

---

## Quick Reference: Automation Vocabulary  

- **Automation Center** – The sidebar where you create, view, and manage all board automations.  
- **Trigger** – The event that starts an automation (e.g., “When status changes”).  
- **Action** – The response the automation performs (e.g., “Notify someone”).  
- **Rule Builder** – The visual interface that lets you link triggers to actions.  
- **Pulse** – Monday.com’s internal term for an item (used in dynamic placeholders like `{{pulse.name}}`).  
- **Toggle Switch** – The on/off control for each automation.  

---

## Putting It All Together: A Mini‑Project  

Create a **“Weekly Review”** board that tracks three recurring tasks: **“Update Dashboard,” “Send Summary Email,”** and **“Archive Old Items.”**  

1. **Add a “Week” date column** and set the date for each Monday.  
2. **Create three automations:**  
   - **Trigger:** *When “Week” is today* → **Action:** *Set “Status” to “Ready.”*  
   - **Trigger:** *When “Status” changes to “Ready”* → **Action:** *Notify the team lead.*  
   - **Trigger:** *When “Status” changes to “Done”* → **Action:** *Move item to “Completed Tasks” group.*  

Test the workflow by advancing the board’s date (use the **“Set date”** feature) and watching the automations cascade. This hands‑on exercise reinforces the concepts of triggers, actions, and managing multiple automations on a single board.

---

## Best Practices for Beginners  

- **Start simple.** Build one automation at a time and verify it works before adding more.  
- **Name your automations.** Click the automation’s three‑dot menu → **Rename** to give a clear description (e.g., “Notify Lead on Done”). This makes future audits easier.  
- **Leverage placeholders.** Use `{{pulse.column_name}}` to insert dynamic data into notifications, keeping messages relevant.  
- **Document in a board note.** Add a **Text column** or **Board description** that lists active automations and their purpose.  
- **Regularly review.** Schedule a monthly “Automation Health Check” to prune unused rules and adjust thresholds.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions  

**Q: Can I have more than one automation trigger the same action?**  
A: Yes, but it may produce duplicate notifications. Use the “Only once per item” option when available, or consolidate triggers.

**Q: Do automations work on mobile apps?**  
A: All automations run on the server side, so they fire regardless of whether you’re on desktop or mobile. However, push notifications depend on your mobile app settings.

**Q: Are there limits on how many automations I can create?**  
A: The number of automations per board isn’t hard‑capped, but performance may degrade on very large boards. The free and Basic plans have fewer pre‑built automation recipes; higher tiers unlock more templates.

**Q: Can I test an automation without affecting real data?**  
A: Yes. Use a **sandbox board** (duplicate your current board) to experiment. The automation behaves exactly the same, but any changes stay isolated.

---

## Next Steps  

Now that you’ve mastered the basics of creating, editing, and managing automations, you’re ready to explore **Integrations** (Chapter 7). There you’ll learn how to connect Monday.com with external tools like email, Slack, and Google Calendar—extending the power of automations beyond the platform itself.

---

## Key Takeaways  

- **Automation = Trigger + Action.** It lets Monday.com perform routine tasks automatically.  
- **Why automate?** Saves time, reduces errors, and keeps teams aligned without manual hand‑offs.  
- **Create a basic automation:** Use the Automation Center → “When status changes to Done → then notify [user].”  
- **Manage automations:** View, enable/disable, edit, duplicate, or delete them from the Automation Center.  
- **Best practices:** Start simple, name rules, use placeholders, document on the board, and audit regularly.  

With these foundations, you can begin building smarter, more efficient workflows that let Monday.com do the heavy lifting for you.

modules.title: 7. Integrations Basics
modules.content:
## Why Integrations Matter: A Real‑World Snapshot  

Imagine Maya, a product‑development lead, juggling three tools every day:  

* **Google Drive** for design assets  
* **Slack** for rapid team updates  
* **Outlook** for milestone meetings  

When Maya adds a new feature request to her Monday.com board, she wants the related design mock‑up automatically linked, a Slack channel alerted, and the delivery date reflected on her Outlook calendar—without manual copy‑pasting. The ability to *integrate* these apps turns a collection of isolated systems into a single, fluid workflow.  

In this chapter you’ll discover the most beginner‑friendly integrations, walk through attaching a Google Drive file to an item, and learn quick fixes for the hiccups that often appear the first time you connect tools.

---

## 1. Popular Beginner‑Friendly Integrations  

| Integration | Core Benefit | Typical Use‑Case |
|------------|--------------|------------------|
| **Google Drive** | Store and retrieve files directly from Monday.com items | Attach design mock‑ups, specs, or contracts |
| **Slack** | Push real‑time notifications to channels or direct messages | Alert the dev team when a task moves to “Ready for Review” |
| **Outlook (Microsoft 365)** | Sync calendar events and email threads | Create a meeting when a deadline is set, or log an email conversation |
| **Microsoft Teams** | Similar to Slack but for organizations already on Teams | Post board updates to a Teams channel |
| **Zapier** | Bridge to over 2,000 other apps (e.g., Trello, Asana) | Create a Zap that adds a new Monday.com item when a Google Form is submitted |

*These five cover the majority of everyday needs for beginners. You can explore many more from the **Integrations Center** later, but mastering these will already give you a powerful, connected workspace.*

---

## 2. Setting Up a Simple Integration: Attach a Google Drive File  

Below is a step‑by‑step guide that builds on the board you created in **Chapter 3** (Building Your First Board). No new terminology is introduced—only actions you can perform directly in the Monday.com interface.

### 2.1. Prerequisites  

1. A **Google account** with the file you intend to attach stored in Google Drive.  
2. At least **one column** on your board that can hold a file link (e.g., a **File** column). If you haven’t added one yet, open the board, click **+ Add Column**, and select **File**.

### 2.2. Walkthrough  

1. **Open the Integrations Center**  
   * From any board, click the **Integrations** button (puzzle‑piece icon) located in the top‑right toolbar.  

2. **Choose the Google Drive Integration**  
   * In the search bar, type “Google Drive” and select the **“When a file is added to a specific folder, create an item”** recipe, or the reverse “When an item is created, attach a Google Drive file.” For this scenario, pick the latter.  

3. **Connect Your Google Account**  
   * A pop‑up will ask you to **Sign in with Google**. Use the same email that holds the file you want to link.  
   * Grant Monday.com the requested permissions (read‑only is enough for attaching files).  

4. **Map the Fields**  
   * **Trigger** – *When an item is created* (or when a specific column changes).  
   * **Action** – *Attach a file from Google Drive*.  
   * Click the **“Choose a file”** field and navigate to the folder where your design file lives. Optionally, enable **“Search by file name”** if you want Monday.com to pull the most recent version automatically.  

5. **Select the Destination Column**  
   * In the **“Attach to column”** dropdown, choose the **File** column you added earlier. This tells Monday.com where the link will appear on the item.  

6. **Activate the Integration**  
   * Click **Add to Board** and then **Turn On**. A green toggle confirms the recipe is live.  

7. **Test It**  
   * Create a new item on the board (e.g., “New Landing Page Design”).  
   * The integration should instantly populate the File column with the selected Google Drive document. Verify by clicking the file icon; it should open the file in Google Drive.  

### 2.3. Quick Checklist  

- ✅ Google account connected  
- ✅ File column present on the board  
- ✅ Correct folder/file selected in the recipe  
- ✅ Integration toggle turned **On**  

If any step fails, refer to the troubleshooting tips in Section 4.

---

## 3. Extending the Basics: Slack and Outlook Integrations  

### 3.1. Slack – Instant Team Alerts  

| Goal | Example Recipe | How It Works |
|------|----------------|--------------|
| Notify a channel when a status changes | “When a status changes to **Done**, send a message to a Slack channel” | Monday.com watches the **Status** column; once it flips to *Done*, a predefined message (e.g., “✅ Feature X completed”) is posted to the chosen Slack channel. |

**Setup Steps (30 seconds)**  

1. Click **Integrations** → search **Slack** → select the desired recipe.  
2. **Connect** your Slack workspace (you’ll be redirected to Slack to authorize Monday.com).  
3. Choose the **channel** (or DM) and map the **status column** you want to monitor.  
4. Turn the integration **On** and test by changing an item’s status.

**Tip:** Use **@mentions** in the message template (e.g., `@here`) to draw immediate attention.

### 3.2. Outlook – Calendar Sync  

| Goal | Example Recipe | How It Works |
|------|----------------|--------------|
| Create a calendar event when a date column is set | “When a date is set, create an Outlook calendar event” | Monday.com reads the **Date** column; it then creates an Outlook event with the item’s name as the title and optional description fields. |

**Setup Steps (1‑2 minutes)**  

1. Open **Integrations**, search **Outlook**, and pick the “Create an event” recipe.  
2. **Authorize** your Microsoft 365 account.  
3. Map the **Date** column to the event’s **Start Date** (and optionally an **End Date** column).  
4. Choose the **Calendar** (default or a specific one) where the event should appear.  
5. Turn the integration **On**.  

**Test:** Set a date on an item (e.g., “Launch Review – 2024‑09‑15”). Check your Outlook calendar for a new entry titled “Launch Review”.

---

## 4. Troubleshooting Common Integration Issues  

Even the simplest integrations can stumble. Below are the most frequent roadblocks and concise fixes.

### 4.1. “Connection Failed” or “Authorization Error”  

- **Cause:** The external app (Google, Slack, Outlook) is linked to a different user than the one currently logged into Monday.com.  
- **Fix:**  
  1. In the **Integrations Center**, click the gear icon next to the integration.  
  2. **Disconnect** the existing account.  
  3. Re‑connect using the **same email** you use for the external service.  

### 4.2. File Not Appearing After Google Drive Integration  

- **Cause 1:** The selected file resides in a **private folder** not shared with the Monday.com service account.  
- **Fix:** Share the folder (or file) with the email address shown in the integration’s permission screen (often something like `monday-integration@googleusercontent.com`).  

- **Cause 2:** The board lacks a **File column** or the column is hidden.  
- **Fix:** Add a **File** column (or unhide it via the **Column Settings** menu).  

### 4.3. Slack Messages Not Sending  

- **Cause:** The Slack channel selected no longer exists (renamed or archived).  
- **Fix:** Re‑open the integration, click the channel dropdown, and select the updated channel.  

- **Cause:** The Slack app was **removed** from the workspace after the initial connection.  
- **Fix:** Re‑install the Monday.com Slack app from the Slack App Directory, then reconnect.  

### 4.4. Outlook Calendar Events Missing  

- **Cause:** The **date column** contains an invalid date format (e.g., “next Friday” instead of a proper calendar date).  
- **Fix:** Ensure the column is set to the **Date** type and entry follows the `YYYY‑MM‑DD` format or uses the calendar picker.  

- **Cause:** The Outlook account lacks **calendar write permissions**.  
- **Fix:** In Microsoft 365, ask your admin to grant the Monday.com app “Can edit” rights on the target calendar.  

### 4.5. General “Integration Not Triggering”  

1. **Check the Trigger Conditions** – Verify that the recipe’s *when* clause matches the action you performed (e.g., status change vs. item creation).  
2. **Confirm Column Visibility** – Hidden columns can prevent the integration from reading data.  
3. **Review Automation Conflicts** – If you have automations that modify the same column, they may fire before or after the integration, affecting outcomes. Temporarily disable conflicting automations to isolate the issue.  

**Pro Tip:** The **Integration Log** (found under **Board Settings → Integrations → View Log**) shows timestamps and any error messages, making diagnosis faster.

---

## 5. Best Practices for First‑Time Integrations  

- **Start Small:** Activate one integration at a time. This isolates variables and simplifies troubleshooting.  
- **Use Descriptive Column Names:** Clear names like “Design File (Google Drive)” or “Launch Date (Outlook)” help you map fields accurately.  
- **Document Credentials:** Keep a secure note of which Google/Slack/Outlook accounts are linked to Monday.com, especially if you manage multiple workspaces.  
- **Set Permissions Wisely:** Grant the minimum required access (read‑only for Google Drive, write for Outlook calendar) to reduce security risk.  
- **Test with a Dummy Item:** Before rolling out to the whole team, create a test item that mimics a real scenario.  

---

## Key Takeaways  

- **Integrations turn Monday.com into a hub**, connecting files, chat, and calendars without manual copying.  
- **Google Drive, Slack, and Outlook** are the most approachable integrations for beginners; each follows a similar three‑step pattern: choose a recipe, connect the external account, map fields.  
- **Attaching a Google Drive file** requires a File column, a connected Google account, and a correctly configured recipe.  
- **Common issues**—authorization mismatches, permission gaps, hidden columns—can be resolved quickly by revisiting the connection settings and ensuring proper sharing.  
- **Best practice**: add integrations one at a time, use clear column names, and always test with a dummy item before full deployment.  

By mastering these fundamentals, you’ll spend less time toggling between apps and more time moving work forward—all within the familiar interface you’ve already built in earlier chapters.

modules.title: 8. Collaboration & Communication Tools
modules.content:
## Posting Updates and @‑Mentioning Teammates  

### What an “Update” Is  

In Monday.com an **Update** is a short, time‑stamped message that lives directly on an item (the row you created in *Building Your First Board*). Think of it as a mini‑conversation thread attached to a specific task, bug, or feature. Updates keep all the chatter about that item in one place, so you don’t have to chase emails or jump between chats.

> **Why it matters:** When a designer uploads a new mock‑up, a developer can comment “Looks good – I’ll start coding tomorrow” right on the same item. Everyone sees the context instantly.

### Where to Find the Update Box  

1. Open the board that contains the item you want to discuss.  
2. Click the item’s **cell** (any column) to open the item’s detail pane on the right side of the screen.  
3. At the bottom of this pane you’ll see a gray bar that says **“Write an update…”** – that’s the entry field.

If you’ve already expanded the pane in a previous session, the field will be visible the moment the pane opens.

### Writing an Effective Update  

| Step | Action | Tip |
|------|--------|-----|
| 1 | **Start with a clear subject** – Monday.com automatically captures the first line as a preview in the board view. | Example: “🚀 Launch assets ready for review” |
| 2 | **State the purpose** – “I’ve uploaded the final branding pack.” | Keep it to one‑two sentences. |
| 3 | **Add any required next steps** – “Please approve by EOD Friday.” | Use bold (`**bold**`) for deadlines or important actions. |
| 4 | **End with a call‑to‑action** – “@JaneDoe, can you take a look?” | This leads naturally into the @‑mention step. |

### Using @‑Mentions  

An **@‑mention** is a way to notify a specific teammate (or a whole team) that their attention is needed. When you type `@` followed by a name, Monday.com suggests matching users; click the right one and the name turns blue.

- **@‑mentioning a person** – Sends them a notification (email, in‑app, or mobile push, depending on their personal settings).  
- **@‑mentioning a team** – Use `@TeamName` to notify every member of that team. Great for cross‑functional work (e.g., “@MarketingTeam, please add the social copy”).  

**Best practice:** Mention only the people who truly need to act. Over‑mentioning can lead to notification fatigue.

### Quick Checklist for Posting Updates  

- [ ] Is the update attached to the correct item?  
- [ ] Have you used an @‑mention for anyone who needs to respond?  
- [ ] Did you include a clear deadline or next step?  
- [ ] Have you attached any supporting files (next section) if needed?  

---

## Attaching Files and Embedding Links  

### Adding Files to an Update  

1. In the same Update box, click the **paperclip icon** (📎).  
2. Choose **“Upload from computer”**, **“Google Drive”**, **“Dropbox”**, or another connected service (see *Integrations Basics* for how those connections work).  
3. Select the file(s) and click **Open**.  

Monday.com supports common formats such as PDFs, images (PNG, JPG), spreadsheets (XLSX), and many others. The **file size limit** for a single upload is 250 MB on the Free plan and higher on paid tiers. If you hit a limit, consider sharing a link instead (see next subsection).

### Embedding Links Within Updates  

If the file is already hosted online (e.g., a design prototype on Figma), you can embed the link directly:

- Type or paste the URL into the update text. Monday.com automatically creates a **preview card** showing the title, thumbnail, and a clickable “Open” button.  
- To keep the update tidy, you can hide the raw URL by selecting the text and clicking the **link icon** (🔗) to turn it into a hyperlink.  

**Example:**  

```
Here’s the latest prototype: https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/Launch‑Mockup
```

Monday.com will render a preview that looks like a mini‑card, making it easy for teammates to click through without leaving the platform.

### Viewing and Downloading Attachments  

- **Hover** over a file thumbnail to see a quick “Download” button.  
- **Click** the file name to open it in a new tab (if the browser supports the format).  
- Attachments are also listed in the **Activity Log** (next section), so you can trace who added what and when.

### Best Practices for File Management  

- **Name files clearly** before uploading (e.g., `Launch_Brand_Assets_v2.pdf`).  
- **Group related files** in a folder on your cloud storage and share the folder link instead of uploading dozens of individual files.  
- **Delete old versions** when they become obsolete to avoid clutter. You can do this from the item’s detail pane—click the three‑dot menu next to the attachment and select **Delete**.  

---

## Tracking Changes with the Activity Log  

### What the Activity Log Shows  

Every board in Monday.com has an **Activity Log** (sometimes called “History”). It records:

- **Updates** you post (including @‑mentions).  
- **File uploads** and deletions.  
- **Column changes** (e.g., status moved from “In Progress” to “Done”).  
- **Automation runs** (e.g., “When status changes to Done, move item to Archive”).  

Think of it as a chronological audit trail that anyone with access to the board can view.

### Accessing the Activity Log  

1. Open the board you’re working on.  
2. In the top‑right corner of the board view, click the **clock icon** (🕒) – this opens the Activity Log pane.  
3. The pane slides in from the right, showing entries in reverse‑chronological order.  

You can also view the log for a **single item** by opening its detail pane and clicking the **“Activity”** tab at the top of the pane.

### Understanding Log Entries  

Each entry contains:

- **Timestamp** – When the action occurred.  
- **User avatar** – Who performed the action.  
- **Action description** – E.g., “John added an update”, “File ‘Specs.pdf’ uploaded”, “Status changed to ‘Review’”.  
- **Context** – The name of the item the action relates to.  

For updates, the full text (including any @‑mentions) is displayed, so you can read the exact conversation without opening the item.

### Filtering and Searching the Log  

The Activity Log includes a **search bar** at the top. You can type keywords such as:

- A teammate’s name (`Jane`) to see everything they’ve done.  
- A file extension (`.pdf`) to locate all PDF uploads.  
- A status value (`Done`) to track when items moved into that column.  

There are also **filter dropdowns** for:

- **Date range** – Today, Last 7 days, Custom range.  
- **Action type** – Updates, File uploads, Column changes, Automations.  

These filters help you quickly answer questions like “Who approved the budget last week?” or “Which items had files added yesterday?”

### Using the Log for Accountability  

Because every change is timestamped, the Activity Log becomes a natural **accountability tool**:

- **Project managers** can verify that deadlines were met.  
- **Team leads** can spot bottlenecks (e.g., many items stuck in “In Review”).  
- **Stakeholders** can see a transparent record of progress without needing separate status reports.  

If you need to **revert a change**, many column edits can be undone directly from the log (click the three‑dot menu on the entry and choose **“Undo”**). For updates, you can edit or delete the message just like any other post.

---

## Putting It All Together: A Mini Workflow  

### Scenario  

Your team is preparing the launch of a new mobile app. The board is called **“App Launch – Sprint 5”** (created in *Building Your First Board*). The key items include:

1. **Design assets** – status column “Ready/Review/Approved”.  
2. **Marketing copy** – status column “Draft/Review/Final”.  
3. **App store screenshots** – status column “In Progress/Ready”.  

You, as the project coordinator, need to:

- Notify the design team that the brand guidelines have been updated.  
- Share the new logo file with the marketing team.  
- Track when each item moves to “Approved” so you can schedule the release date.

### Step‑by‑Step Execution  

1. **Open the “Design assets” item** and click the detail pane.  
2. In the **Update box**, type:  

   ```
   🎨 New brand guidelines uploaded – please review by **Wednesday 10 AM**.
   @DesignTeam
   ```  

   Click the **paperclip icon**, upload `Brand_Guidelines_v3.pdf`, then hit **Send**.  

3. **Switch to the “Marketing copy” item**. In its Update box, write:  

   ```
   📄 Updated copy draft attached. Let’s aim for final version by **Friday**.
   @MarketingTeam
   ```  

   Attach the Word document `App_Copy_Draft.docx`.  

4. As the design lead marks the status to **“Approved”**, the **Activity Log** automatically records:  

   - “Design lead changed status to Approved on ‘Design assets’.”  

5. **Later, you open the Activity Log**, filter by **“Status changes”** and **date range “Last 2 days.”** You see the approval entry and can confirm the timeline.  

6. **If a stakeholder asks for proof**, you can share the specific Activity Log entry or simply copy‑paste the update text (which already includes the @‑mentions and file links).  

Through this loop, every conversation, file, and status move stays attached to the relevant item, eliminating scattered emails and ensuring a single source of truth.

---

## Common Pitfalls and Quick Fixes  

| Pitfall | Why It Happens | Quick Fix |
|---------|----------------|-----------|
| **Forgot to @‑mention** | Updates are posted but teammates never see the notification. | After posting, edit the update (three‑dot menu ► **Edit**) and add the missing @‑mention. |
| **Uploading the wrong file version** | Multiple drafts get mixed up, especially when file names are generic. | Adopt a naming convention (e.g., `v1`, `v2`) before uploading. Use the **Delete** option to remove outdated attachments. |
| **Activity Log looks empty** | The board’s permission settings hide history from certain roles. | Verify that the user’s role includes “View Activity” (Admin → **Board Settings** → **Permissions**). |
| **Too many notifications** | Over‑mentioning or posting updates on every tiny change. | Consolidate related changes into a single update; use the **“Add comment”** field for brief notes that don’t need full notifications. |
| **File size exceeds limit** | Trying to upload a high‑resolution video on a Free plan. | Upload to a linked cloud storage (Google Drive, Dropbox) and share the link instead of the raw file. |

---

## Key Takeaways  

- **Updates** keep conversations anchored to specific items; use the Update box in the item detail pane.  
- **@‑mentions** notify the right people—type `@` followed by a name or team to trigger in‑app, email, or push alerts.  
- **File attachments** are added via the paperclip icon; embed external links for large or frequently‑updated assets.  
- The **Activity Log** records every update, file upload, status change, and automation run; access it via the clock icon or the item’s “Activity” tab.  
- Filtering and searching the Activity Log let you audit progress, verify approvals, and maintain accountability without leaving Monday.com.  

By mastering these collaboration tools, you turn your Monday.com board from a static checklist into a living, transparent workspace where every stakeholder stays in the loop and every piece of work is traceable.
